newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's BGZ bank 1996 gross rises to PLN 495 mln. [CORRECTED 14:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Poland's BGZ bank 1996 gross rises to PLN 495 mln. [CORRECTED 14:47 GMT]

text.p: The gross profit of the Polish cooperative Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) rose 37.1 percent last year to 495.4 million zlotys against 1995, BGZ's deputy president Wladyslaw Kulczycki said on Thursday.
(Corrects to show gross profit rose to 495.4 million zlotys last year, not "from" 495.4 million zlotys in 1995.)

"Our 1996 results are very good because we managed to retrieve more bad debts than we initially thought. We expect a gross profit of about 500 million zlotys in 1997," Kulczycki told a news conference.
He said it was too early to say what the bank's net profit had been.

Kulczycki said some 20 percent of the gross profit resulted from the two billion zloty injection from the treasury in the form of bonds, which the bank secured to restructure its huge bad debt portfolio inherited from the communist era.
The gross profit was mainly boosted by a 120 percent jump in revenueus from banking operations, notably interest, a BGZ report presented by Kulczycki said.
It said revenues from reserves halved against 1995 which was a "quality change" in the structure of its financial results.
Kulczycki said the amount of bad debt shrank in BGZ's credit portfoilio to 29.2 percent in 1996 from 42.3 percent in 1995.
BGZ's capital eased 6.3 percent in 1996 to 1.502 billion zlotys and its gross balance sheet rose 20 percent to 13.952 billion zlotys.
